name: Jamie Oliver's Chicken in Milk {Seriously Delish}
writer_notes: Ingredient-vs-step coverage verified both directions: chicken, salt, black pepper, olive oil, ground cinnamon, fresh sage, lemon zest, garlic, and milk are each used by a step; no step references anything not on the buy list.
Cinnamon in the source is '1/2 stick'; the locked buy line converts it to '1 3/4 teaspoons ground cinnamon', so the method says ground cinnamon to match the buy string, not a stick.
Lemons are zest only per the source and locked line; prose never calls for juice or flesh.

No cost_lines or cost_ps value was supplied in this dispatch, so shop_smart makes only package-size statements (half gallon = 8 cups milk, garlic by the head/bag, sage by the bunch) and avoids per-ounce, leftover, or lasts-several-batches claims that cannot be traced.
The only numbers in prose are the locked macros (693 cal, 57g protein, 10g carbs, 46.2g fat), the 14 servings, oven temp/time straight from the source, and the ${{cost_ps}} token.
intro_html:
Here is a dish that sounds like a mistake and eats like a secret. You brown a whole chicken, then you pour milk over it and let the oven do something strange and wonderful. The milk breaks into soft curds, the lemon zest and garlic and sage fold in, and what comes out is chicken so tender it barely needs a knife, sitting in a sauce that tastes like nobody should be able to make it this cheap. Jamie Oliver gets the credit, and RecipeTin Eats earns the trust. We just scaled it up so your whole week eats like a Sunday.

The numbers are the quiet flex. Each of the 14 servings lands at 693 calories with 57 grams of protein, only 10 grams of carbs, and 46.2 grams of fat. That is a rich, satisfying plate that still clears every rail we set: high protein, low carb, real food. You are not eating diet food here. You are eating a proper roast that happens to be built for the week.
ingredients_display: Whole Chicken (generic (USDA)): 3 whole chickens, about 3 3/4 lb each (11 1/2 lb total) (5250 g)
Salt (Morton): 2 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste (42 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): 2 tablespoons black pepper (14 g)
Ground Cinnamon (Great Value): 1 3/4 teaspoons ground cinnamon (5 g)
Fresh Sage: scant 1 cup loosely packed fresh sage leaves (18 g)
Garlic: 35 garlic cloves, whole, skin on (105 g)
Milk (store brand): 8 cups low fat milk (1929 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Whole Chicken, 3 whole chickens, about 3 3/4 lb each (11 1/2 lb total): ~$15.28. Buy 12 lbs: $15.84.
Olive Oil, 7 tablespoons olive oil: ~$1.02. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Fresh Sage, scant 1 cup loosely packed fresh sage leaves: ~$3.16. Buy 1 0.7oz clamshell: $3.51.
Garlic, 35 garlic cloves, whole, skin on: ~$1.43. Buy 3 heads: $1.74.
Milk, 8 cups low fat milk: ~$1.44. Buy 1 gallon: $2.82.
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper, ground cinnamon): ~$0.53. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $26.03 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.86 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $28.63 across 14 servings, roughly $2.04 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $10.37 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $39.00. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: Whole chickens and a half gallon of milk is about as lean as a grocery list gets, and it turns into 14 dinners that taste like you fussed. At ${{cost_ps}} per serving, this is the kind of math that makes meal prep feel less like a chore and more like a raise. You are buying humble ingredients and cooking your way into something that eats far above its price tag.
shop_smart:
Buy three whole chickens, right around 3 3/4 pounds each, which puts you at about 11 1/2 pounds of bird for the batch. Whole chickens are almost always the cheapest way to buy real chicken, and here the whole bird is the point, so there is no trimming waste to pay for. If your store runs a sale on the family pack of whole birds, that is your green light.

The milk is the other star and it is stupid cheap. You need 8 cups of low fat milk, which is exactly one half gallon carton, so you are buying a single container and using it. Grab the store brand; there is no premium milk on earth that will make this sauce better.

The rest is pantry and produce. You want a whole head or a small bag of garlic to hit 35 cloves left in their skins, 7 lemons for zest only, and a bunch of fresh sage. Buy the sage by the bunch or one large clamshell rather than the tiny herb packet, because a scant cup of loosely packed leaves adds up fast. Ground cinnamon, olive oil, salt, and black pepper are almost certainly already in your cupboard.
make_it:
Heat your oven to 375F. Pat all three chickens dry with paper towels, because dry skin is what browns. Sprinkle the salt and a good few grinds of black pepper all over each bird and press it in, working the top and sides.

Get a heavy based pot hot over high heat and add the olive oil. Brown the chickens all over as best you can, one at a time if that is what your pot allows. The trick from the original still stands: tongs stuck in the rear of the bird and a wooden spoon to lift and tilt, so you get color on the skin without tearing it. This step is where the flavor is born, so do not rush it.

Pour off the excess fat once the birds are browned. If wrestling a whole chicken while draining a hot pot is not your idea of fun, lift the chicken onto a plate first, drain the fat, then return it. Now add everything else straight into the pot with the chicken: the ground cinnamon, the fresh sage, the lemon zest, all 35 garlic cloves in their skins, and the 8 cups of milk.

Bake covered for 40 minutes, then uncover and bake another 50 minutes, so 1 hour and 30 minutes of oven time in total. The milk will look curdled and broken, and that is exactly right; those curds are the good part. Let the birds stand about 5 minutes before you lift them out. Do not strain the sauce. You want the curds, the softened garlic, and the bits of sage going into every container.
portion_html:
Pull the chickens out, let them rest, then carve the meat off the bones. Three birds gives you plenty of meat to split evenly across 14 containers. Weigh your empty pot before you start, then weigh the meat and sauce so you can divide by 14 and hit the same portion every time; that is the honest way to make sure container one and container fourteen are the same meal.

Spoon that broken milk sauce over each portion, garlic and curds and sage included. Each container lands at 693 calories with 57 grams of protein and just 10 grams of carbs, so it plays nicely with rice, roasted potatoes, or a pile of green vegetables added the day you eat it.

head.description: Jamie Oliver's Chicken in Milk scaled to 14 meal-prep servings. Whole chicken braised in milk with lemon zest, garlic, sage, and cinnamon. 693 calories and 57g protein per serving, low carb and budget friendly.

recipeIngredient: Whole Chicken, 3 whole chickens, about 3 3/4 lb each (11 1/2 lb total) (5250 g)
Salt, 2 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste (42 g)
Black Pepper, 2 tablespoons black pepper (14 g)
Olive Oil, 7 tablespoons olive oil (94 g)
Ground Cinnamon, 1 3/4 teaspoons ground cinnamon (5 g)

Milk (store brand), 8 cups low fat milk (1929 g)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375F. Pat the whole chickens dry with paper towels.
Sprinkle the salt and several grinds of black pepper all over each chicken, pressing it into the top and sides.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy based pot over high heat.
Brown the chickens all over, using tongs and a wooden spoon to lift and tilt each bird so the skin colors without tearing.
Pour off the excess fat from the pot, lifting the chicken out onto a plate first if that is easier, then return it.
Add the ground cinnamon, fresh sage, lemon zest, garlic cloves, and milk to the pot with the chicken.
Bake covered for 40 minutes, then uncovered for 50 minutes, 1 hour 30 minutes total.
Let the chicken stand about 5 minutes, then carve and serve with the unstrained milk sauce, curds, garlic, and sage.
